question: Does the Hydra delegate translate MaterialX Standard Surface networks into the existing material IR, so that a committed MaterialX fixture extracts to its mirror and matches its reference headless and through Hydra, and the surveyed MaterialX assets render their authored materials?

procedure.reference: lotus-headless --write-material-reference <scratch directory>: every fixture in a cleared GPU scene, BSDF sampling from sample index 0, 4096 spp mean and 64x64 variance; the five existing fixtures' files compared with cmp, then the new fixture's two files adopted
procedure.headless_check: ost build --profile lookdev --intent hydra and ost build (core): each post-build report's renderer.material.fixtures
procedure.hydra: ctest -R 'lotus-renderer-hydra-material(-fixtures)?(-gpu)?$' and ctest -R hydra -LE gpu in build/cy2026-windows-x86_64-py313-lookdev--hydra; no object had zero recorded dependencies before or after the builds
procedure.scripts: python -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'; python scripts/material_fixtures.py check; python scripts/check_docs.py
procedure.survey_assets: usdrecord --renderer Lotus with the change installed to a scratch prefix, and usdrecord --renderer GL with an empty plugin path as the Storm control, on OpenChessSet, StandardShaderBall (authored camera) and MaterialXTest; local overrides added a camera and a uniform dome to OpenChessSet, and blocked the shader-ball ground's outputs:mtlx:surface for Storm

fixture_sha256_note: the USD file as the generator writes it, with LF line endings; it reuses the committed PNG images

warnings: Lotus ignores /MaterialMtlx/Looks/Lobes inputs its material cannot represent: coat, sheen, transmission
Lotus uses the defaults of /MaterialMtlx/Looks/Untranslated inputs whose shader graph it does not translate: base_color

byte_identical: headless wavefront NEE/MIS statistics equal the reference integrator's at 16 and 256 spp
each Hydra image (NEE/MIS and BSDF, 256 spp) is the backend's image of the mirror bit for bit

audit.network_selection: fixed; the delegate requests the mtlx render context
audit.precedence: decided; a MaterialX surface wins over a UsdPreviewSurface, as in Storm
audit.defaults_and_weights: as documented; base colour 0.8 and roughness 0.2; base and emission multiply their colours and a lookup's scale, bias and fallback
audit.metalness_roughness_ior: as documented; clamped as for UsdPreviewSurface
audit.specular_weight: as documented; 0 sets ior 1, other weights except 1 warn
audit.unrepresented_lobes: as documented; ignored with one warning per material
audit.images_and_colour_spaces: as documented; srgb_* is sRGB, anything else raw; Hio texels exact
audit.address_modes_and_coordinates: as documented; periodic by default, constant transparent black, st unless connected
audit.normal_maps: as documented; scale 2 and bias -1, x and y times scale
audit.untranslated_graphs: as documented; default kept, input warned, image not decoded

OpenChessSet.before: 49 'no surface terminal' warnings, default grey everywhere
OpenChessSet.after: authored base colour, metalness, roughness and normal maps on every mesh

StandardShaderBall.before: 4 'no surface terminal' warnings; even grey ground
StandardShaderBall.after: numbered ground grid; example materials translated

MaterialXTest.after: brass translated with a coat warning; its roughness image path resolves to ./textures/./textures/brass_roughness.jpg, which neither renderer opens

survey_assets.shader_ball_ground: st spans t from 0 to -1; the UsdPreviewSurface lookup's useMetadata wraps read black in Lotus; the MaterialX ND_image repeats by default; Storm with the MaterialX output blocked shows no grid; the 7500x7500 half EXR decodes

not_run: the full Hydra CTest suite and the viewport, research and ci-core trees
usdview and the installed Hydra host with the fixture
survey stages other than the three MaterialX ones
